messages.subject: CANTAB gamble task model
parts:
Hi,


I have been working through some of the models from this paper: ‘A computational model of the Cambridge gambling task with applications to substance use disorders’ 

https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0376871619304880#sec0070

 

I am unclear on the equations governing the bet valuation function from the supplementary material shown here:


     

 

 

For these models x is the cumulative total, so it is not possible for it be negative, in contrast to the text above. I interpreted x > 0 to mean a win and x < 0 to mean a loss in order to resolve this, but wanted to confirm that this is how the models were intended to be implemented?


Thanks,

Ani

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: CANTAB gamble task model
parts:
Hi Ani,

Thanks for reaching out! 

And yes, I see now that the notation is misleading in the supplement—your interpretation is correct. For the cumulative model, it is always the non-negative, cumulative total being evaluated. Which valuation function is used depends only on if the cumulative amount is decreasing (i.e. a "loss") or increasing (i.e. a "win"). 

Let me know if that is clear now, and thanks for the catch! 

Best,
Nate
